name: usgs_palo_alto_1961_24k
source: USGS 1:24,000 Palo Alto, CA 7.5' quadrangle, 1961 edition, TNM item 293908
projection: Polyconic, Clarke 1866 / NAD27, lon0=-122.1879999999992, from the GeoTIFF tags (tiepoint -6641.66,4152527.39; 2.0320 m/px). Bilinear interpolation of the 4 neat-line corners is accurate to a few px inside the quad.
formula: Coordinates printed on the map are NAD27. For modern (WGS84) lon/lat add lon+0.00108, lat+0.00004 first, then u=(lon-lon_w)/(lon_e-lon_w); v=(lat_n-lat)/(lat_n-lat_s); x=lerp(lerp(NW.x,NE.x,u),lerp(SW.x,SE.x,u),v); y likewise. 'places' below already include the shift (input WGS84). Verify visually before pinning a tiny point.
